chapter: Joe Liggins and back to Kid Ory
title: Playing with Joe Liggins and the Honeydrippers
summary: At the end of the war Frank Passley and Happy Prince talked Joe into joining Joe Liggins's band, whose blues-and-early-rock style was not his own.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You'd just gone to (?) when you left the Kid Ory band.

I can remember almost the exact date, because Japan had just surrendered -- it was during the war with Japan. In the meantime, I played a little while with Joe Liggins and the Honeydrippers, which wasn't my style, but I knew Frank Passley, and he talked me into it -- him and Happy Prince.
Good old Frank Passley played with them, too?
Oh, I didn't know Frank Passley was with Joe Liggins.
He played with Joe Liggins, and also Happy Prince.
When you say it wasn't your style, what kind of music did they play?
Well, Joe Liggins was more or less the Blues, a little Rock, stuff like that.
Well, that was kind of early for what you say was Rock...
It was the beginning of it. I don't know whether it was Rock Swing or Blues Swing or whatever you'd want to call it...
It wasn't a specific style. But it would be closer to kind of the Rock. Really they didn't call it that, but I would think it was close to it.
Well, was there a market for that kind of stuff around that time?
